cells.question: Q01

passages.quote: together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year.
has trained, or initiated the training of, a frontier model

cells.note: Two defined terms bear the duties: “frontier developer” (§ 22757.11(h)) and “large frontier developer” (§ 22757.11(j)), a frontier developer whose revenues with affiliates exceeded $500 million in the preceding calendar year. The framework duty (§ 22757.12(a)), the transparency-report summaries of risk assessments (§ 22757.12(c)(2)), internal-use summaries (§ 22757.12(d)) and the anonymous internal process (Lab. Code § 1107.1(e)) fall on large frontier developers; the transparency report (§ 22757.12(c)(1)), incident reporting (§ 22757.13(c)) and the anti-retaliation rule (Lab. Code § 1107.1(a)) fall on all frontier developers.

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: “Frontier model” means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations.
together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year.

cells.note: Model threshold: training compute greater than 10^26 operations, which under § 22757.11(i)(2) includes the original training run and subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning or other material modifications. Developer tier: annual gross revenues with affiliates above $500 million in the preceding calendar year. § 22757.14 requires the Department of Technology to recommend, on or before 1 January 2027 and annually thereafter, whether and how to update these definitions; it does not itself change them.

cells.question: Q03

passages.locator: SEC. 2, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(a), opening clause
passages.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework
review and, as appropriate, update its frontier AI framework at least once per year.

cells.note: Applies to large frontier developers. “Frontier AI framework” is defined in § 22757.11(g) as documented technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess and mitigate catastrophic risks; § 22757.12(a)(1)–(10) lists the matters the framework describes, including thresholds, mitigations, third-party assessment, cybersecurity, incident response, internal governance and internal use.

cells.question: Q04

passages.locator: SEC. 2, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(a), opening clause
passages.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework
publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.

cells.note: Publication on the developer’s website; a materially modified framework is published with a justification within 30 days. § 22757.12(f) permits redactions to protect trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety or national security or to comply with law, with the character and justification of each redaction described and the unredacted information retained for five years. No provision requiring the framework itself to be submitted to a public authority was found.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: assess whether a frontier model has capabilities

passages.locator: SEC. 2, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(a), opening clause
passages.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework

cells.note: The framework, which a large frontier developer must implement and comply with, describes how the developer approaches defining and assessing thresholds to identify and assess whether a frontier model has capabilities that could pose a catastrophic risk (§ 22757.12(a)(2)). The text sets no free-standing duty to test each model; § 22757.12(c)(2)(A)–(B) requires summaries of assessments of catastrophic risks conducted pursuant to the framework, and § 22757.12(d) summaries of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use.

setAside.reason: Requires summaries of assessments in the transparency report; it presupposes assessments under the framework rather than imposing them.
Transmission of summaries of any internal-use assessment to the Office of Emergency Services; no duty to assess is stated.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: shall review critical safety incident reports

cells.note: The Office of Emergency Services shall review critical safety incident reports submitted by frontier developers: a review of filings, not of the model. The framework must describe how the developer approaches using third parties to assess catastrophic risks (§ 22757.12(a)(5)), and the transparency report summarises the extent to which third-party evaluators were involved (§ 22757.12(c)(2)(C)); neither requires an outside assessment.

search.read: SEC. 2 in full; SEC. 3 (Gov. Code § 11546.8); SEC. 4.

setAside.reason: Describes the content of the developer’s framework (its approach to using third parties); does not require an outside assessment.
Disclosure of the extent of third-party evaluator involvement; involvement is not required.
Concerns external verifiability of coverage definitions in the Department of Technology’s recommendations, not assessment of a model.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident.

the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction, that is appropriate based on the nature of that incident and as required by law

cells.note: Applies to all frontier developers. Fifteen days from discovery to the Office of Emergency Services; 24 hours to an appropriate authority where the incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. “Critical safety incident” is defined in § 22757.11(d). § 22757.13(h)–(i) provides that compliance with a designated federal law, regulation or guidance document is deemed compliance with the section (see Q15).

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report
every three months or pursuant to another reasonable schedule specified by the large frontier developer and communicated in writing to the Office of Emergency Services

cells.note: Trigger: before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. Contents: website, contact mechanism, release date, languages, output modalities, intended uses and use restrictions (§ 22757.12(c)(1)(A)–(G)); large frontier developers add summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments, results, third-party evaluator involvement and other framework steps (§ 22757.12(c)(2)). Large frontier developers also transmit summaries of internal-use risk assessments to the Office of Emergency Services on the stated schedule (§ 22757.12(d)). No output-labelling duty was seen.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing,
a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information

cells.note: Protection covers “covered employees”, defined in Lab. Code § 1107(b) as employees responsible for assessing, managing or addressing risk of critical safety incidents, who disclose to the Attorney General, a federal authority or persons with authority over the matter information on a specific and substantial danger from a catastrophic risk or a violation of the Act. The internal anonymous process (§ 1107.1(e)) is a duty of large frontier developers; § 1107.1(d) requires notice of rights, and § 1107.1(f)–(h) provide attorney’s fees, a burden-of-proof rule and injunctive relief.

cells.question: Q13

cells.note: Per violation, in an amount dependent on the severity of the violation. § 22757.15(a) names large frontier developers that fail to publish or transmit a compliant document, make a statement in violation of § 22757.12(e), fail to report an incident under § 22757.13 or fail to comply with their own framework. Whistleblower violations (Lab. Code § 1107.1) carry the civil remedies of that section, not this penalty.

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: A civil penalty described in this section shall be recovered in a civil action brought only by the Attorney General.
report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident.

cells.note: The Attorney General recovers civil penalties. The Office of Emergency Services receives incident reports and internal-use summaries, reviews incident reports (§ 22757.13(d)) and may designate equivalent federal standards (§ 22757.13(h)); no penalty power is given to it.

cells.question: Q15

passages.locator: SEC. 2, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(a), opening clause
passages.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework
shall declare its intent to do so to the Office of Emergency Services.
including a system card or model card, shall be deemed in compliance with the applicable paragraph.

cells.note: Requires a developer framework, which describes how the developer approaches incorporating national standards, international standards and industry-consensus best practices (§ 22757.12(a)(1)). A frontier developer that declares its intent to comply with § 22757.13 through a federal law, regulation or guidance document designated by the Office of Emergency Services is “deemed in compliance” with that section to the extent it meets it (§ 22757.13(i)(2)(A)). Publishing transparency-report contents in a system or model card is deemed compliance (§ 22757.12(c)(3)). § 22757.12(c)(4) encourages disclosures consistent with industry best practices.

cells.question: Q01

passages.quote: "Large developer" means a person that has trained at least one frontier model and has spent over one hundred million dollars in compute costs in aggregate in training frontier models.

cells.note: One tier: “large developer”. Accredited colleges and universities engaged in academic research are excluded, and a transferee of full intellectual property rights in a frontier model becomes the large developer (§ 1420(9)). Text as signed in Chapter 699; Chapter 96 of 2026 repeals and re-adds Article 44-B (see ny-ch96).

passages.quote: an artificial intelligence model trained using greater than 10º26 computational operations
the compute cost of which exceeds one hundred million dollars
"Large developer" means a person that has trained at least one frontier model and has spent over one hundred million dollars in compute costs in aggregate in training frontier models.

cells.note: The PDF text layer renders the exponent as “10º26”, i.e. 10^26 operations. Model condition: more than 10^26 operations and compute cost above $100 million; a model produced by knowledge distillation from such a model is also a frontier model where its compute cost exceeds $5 million (§ 1420(6)(b)). Developer condition: over $100 million in aggregate compute costs for training frontier models. § 1424 limits the article to frontier models developed, deployed or operating in whole or in part in New York.

cells.question: Q03

cells.note: “Safety and security protocol” is defined in § 1420(12) (p. 3) as documented technical and organizational protocols describing protections against critical harm, cybersecurity protections, a testing procedure, compliance and senior responsible personnel. § 1421(3) requires an annual review.

cells.question: Q04

passages.quote: Conspicuously publish a copy of the safety and security protocol with appropriate redactions
transmit a copy of such redacted safety and security protocol to the attorney general and division of homeland security and emergency services

cells.note: Before deploying a frontier model. Publication with “appropriate redactions” (defined in § 1420(1)) and transmission of the redacted copy to the attorney general and the division of homeland security and emergency services; § 1421(1)(c)(ii) adds access upon request (see Q06). Material modifications after annual review are published in the same manner (§ 1421(3)).

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: Describe in detail the testing procedure to evaluate if the frontier model poses an unreasonable risk of critical harm
specific tests and test results used in any assessment of the frontier model required by this section or the developer's safety and security protocol

cells.note: The protocol the large developer must implement describes a testing procedure to evaluate whether the model poses an unreasonable risk of critical harm, and the developer must record and retain test information. The text sets no free-standing duty to test each model; § 1421(2) prohibits deployment where it would create an unreasonable risk of critical harm.

setAside.reason: A prohibition on deployment, not a duty to evaluate.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: Grant the attorney general and division of homeland security and emergency services or the attorney general access to the safety and security protocol

cells.note: Access is granted “upon request”, with redactions only as required by federal law: access to a document, with no assessment by the authority required. § 1421(1)(d) requires test records detailed enough for third parties to replicate the testing procedure but does not require a third-party assessment.

setAside.reason: Replicability of tests by third parties is a record-keeping standard; no outside assessment is provided for.
Protocol must enable the developer “or third party” to comply; not an outside assessment.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: A large developer shall disclose each safety incident affecting the frontier model to the attorney general and division of homeland security and emergency services within seventy-two hours

cells.note: Seventy-two hours from learning of the incident or of facts sufficient for a reasonable belief that one occurred. “Safety incident” is defined in § 1420(13). The disclosure includes the date, the reasons the incident qualifies and a short statement.

cells.question: Q08
cells.note: No duty to publish a report on each model, or to draw up and supply model documentation to an authority or to others, was found. Before deploying a frontier model, the large developer must record and retain information on tests and test results for as long as the model is deployed plus five years; retention is set aside below. The published protocol (Q04) is developer-level. No output-labelling duty was seen.

setAside.reason: “specific tests and test results used in any assessment of the frontier model required by this section or the developer's safety and security protocol”: records to be retained, not published or supplied; does not meet the criterion.
Publication and transmission concern the safety and security protocol, not per-model information.
Disclosure of each safety incident to the attorney general and the division of homeland security and emergency services: incident-triggered, recorded under Q07, not a report on each model.
